title: Further Measures to Ensure Affordability of Preschool Education
what_it_is: Further Measures to Ensure Affordability of Preschool Education

sections.label: Preschool enrolment and expenditure rise
sections.summary: Household spending on pre-primary education rose alongside higher preschool enrolment and more children in full-day childcare over half-day kindergarten.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: The increase in household expenditure on pre-primary education corresponds to: one, an overall increase in enrolment of children in preschools; and two, more parents enrolling their children in full-day childcare over half-day kindergarten.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: From 2018 to 2023, the total number of resident children enrolled in childcare centres and kindergartens increased from 157,900 to 167,700.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: The number of children enrolled in childcare centres typically offering full-day programmes increased from 110,200 to 145,400, whereas the number of children enroled in kindergartens typically offering half-day programmes decreased from 47,700 to 22,300.

sections.label: Preschool subsidies and childcare fees
sections.summary: All Singapore Citizen children can get up to $300 basic subsidy, with additional subsidies of $80 to $467 by income tier.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: All Singapore Citizen children can receive up to $300 basic subsidy regardless of their families’ income level.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Families who qualify for additional subsidy receive additional subsidies of $80 to $467 depending on their income tier.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: In 2020, we raised the household income ceiling for additional subsidy from $7,500 to $12,000, and increased the quantum across all eligible income tiers so that more families could benefit from subsidies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Fees for full-day childcare for AOP centres have fallen from $720 in 2022 to $640 in 2025.

sections.label: Preschool share of household income
sections.summary: A median-income household with a child in full-day childcare at an AOP centre spent 3.1% of income in 2023 versus 4.9% in 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: With fee cap reductions and the aforementioned subsidy enhancements, a median-income household with a child attending full-day childcare in an AOP centre spent 3.1% of their household income on preschool in 2023 compared to 4.9% in 2018.
